(§B!§!)The Darod is the largest, most influential Somali clan. They have historically gravitated towards politics, and have produced many rulers and military leaders. Today, they enjoy large political autonomy, for which they are willing to fight.§b

(§B!§!)The Hawiye inhabit the coastal areas of Somalia north of Mogadishu. Through their favorable geographic position the Hawiye controlled trade routes, and as such have a strong tradition of management and bureaucracy. It would be a great blow to the Hawiye if they were removed from administration.§b

(§B!§!)Though their lands are worth little, and their numbers are not great, the Dir are the proudest clan. They claim ancestry from the 7th century, and are known for deeds in Islamic philosophy and theology. Their identity is going to be a tough nut to crack.§b

(§B!§!)Inhabiting Northern Somalia, the Isaaq control a densely populated, though relatively small territory. They are known as the most mercantile of the clans, and to crush them we will have to limit their economic freedoms.§b

(§B!§!)The Rahanweyn live in the fertile valleys of the Jubba and Shebelle rivers, which allows them to practice agriculture. The Geledi clan is a subclan of the Rahanweyn, so we will only have to upturn the other clans - something that can be done by taking reins of agriculture and using our ties within the local nobility to slowly root out the Rahanweyn influence.§b
